Incorporating the Beige Book, conditions across Districts in March–April were modest and mixed: consumer spending was uneven for general retailers and auto dealers; manufacturing faced trade-related uncertainty; and agriculture was pressured by excessive rainfall/flooding. These Beige Book signals reinforce the FOMC’s cautious tone (inflation below 2% with patience on rates) and align with the noted cooling in household spending and business investment. Layering in the April SLOOS’s tighter credit supply and softer demand further tempers the positive tilt. Net: cautious-positive, close to neutral.
